author: christina_rossetti
text:
Why would you, my friend, have come to-day?
O'er these untrod places through the night?
Has some old woman sent her son away,
And left you here alone to wait for him?

Or are your mother and your father dead,
The loved ones who were wont so long ago
To give you up with tears and prayers and dread
When they let you go on foreign lands to roam?

author: edna_millay
text:
I wandered lonely as a cloud
That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
When all at once I saw a crowd,
A host, of golden daffodils;
Beside the lake, beneath the trees,
Fluttering and dancing in the breeze.

Continuous as the stars that shine
And twinkle on the milky way,
They stretched in never-ending line
Along the margin of a bay:
Ten thousand saw I at a glance,
Tossing their heads in sprightly dance.

author: christina_rossetti
text:
When I stumbled over time, when my regrets piled up
My efforts failed, but life continued, as did my faith.
I knew that God would keep me through it all
He would remember me, He would never forsake me
The glory was hidden then, but its promise lay ahead of me.
It lifted me out of myself, out of despair, into love
Into an eternal flame, which has no end or beginning.

author: christina_rossetti
text:
O, ye who turn from me with bitter speech,
As you have not loved, I love you not at all!

And yet, when I am called to stand apart
From that unloving multitude, I recall
The kindly words and looks they gave me oft;
I pity them for their want of true delight,
For their refusal of my proffered hand;
Not all my tears shall quench that grief of theirs.
Yet if they will come back into my life,
They may receive again my warm heart's embrace.

author: edna_millay
text:
The wind was strong, but not as strong as that.

When it had done all she knew how to do.

She took her rest by the stream:
And its edge upon itself reposed;

Like a girl clasped in arms asleep,

Who hath played and is tired out at sea.

author: edna_millay
text:
The little dog lay dead with his eyes closed,
But all the way home he barked to me:
“Where are you going?” I said, “To see
My mother and my father,” who had died;
He said, "I will be coming too.” And so saying,
And that was four years ago this very day.

author: edwin_arlington_robinson
text:
There are three kinds of men in the world,
I know one of them; I'll never be that kind.

He was born with a sense for good and bad,
As if he were always a man on his guard:
His heart is as hard as your stone floor,
And his hands are forever lifting a score.

So you can tell him from afar off by sight --
But let me ask you when have you seen such light?

author: emily_dickinson
text:
I have gone out to learn and bring me home
Knowledge, or at least a good story;
And what I was not able to learn or tell
That is more important than all other things.

What lesson do you take from this stanza? How are they different from the lessons that can be taken from other stanzas of the same poem?

It was not always this way, you see,

author: edwin_arlington_robinson
text: A Heart As I walked down the street one day,I met a stranger who asked me how I was doing. How much easier it is when someone takes an interest in you! But that night I dreamed of you,and remembered my reply with sadness. Then I saw a beggar on the side of the road. He had been beaten by his mother long ago. His father left him when he was young, and he begged his way through life. At last God found him a wife and gave him a home where he might live in peace forevermore

author: edwin_arlington_robinson
text:
My mistress' lips are red, rosy-tipped;
Her navel pits, where milk was pressed, still show
White scars like shells that break against the shore
Where waves once broke on them and lay dead there.
There is no breath between her thighs but air:
And I could swear she would have been a boy
Had he not learned too late to hide his hair

author: emily_dickinson
text:
At the sight of you, my heart is lightened,
For all that I had suffered, and could bear,
In the long day's strife with evil night;
And this new joy will not let me part,
Though through all the world I wander far,
But stay with me to the very end.

Not until we reach heaven shall I leave thee
As God hath bidden--nor when he calls,
Nor yet till he bids farewell from above!

"The Man With The Flower In His Mouth"

An ode to an old man, who for his age is healthy and wise, with a flower in his mouth. 5/8 rhyme scheme; Iambic pentameter

author: edwin_arlington_robinson
text:
In the dim light of an evening sky,
The lovers stood apart, hand-in-hand,
As stars fell like gentle tears across
A tranquil sea of night that did embrace
Their tender hearts and let no cares intrude
Upon the peaceful peace which time bestowed
Upon those two forever held by love,
Each with their own peculiar joys above.

author: emily_dickinson
text:
O God, I love Thee with my whole heart!
I thank Thee for having created me to know
Thee and to give myself unto Thee.
There is no other end of human life;
And yet I live as if there were many things
Which lay beyond it all—as if health, or fame,
Or power were something more than means of service.

text:
The rain is falling, slowly.
We are not sure how long it will last.
It may be some hours or perhaps one day:

And see that they, too, have grown wet with tears;
And even though we say nothing but "yes,"
No words can tell what joy is there for us:
Our hearts are filled with love, all through their veins,

To cool this burning fever on the plains,

author: matthew_arnold
text:
And is it so, that I have left this world?
The golden years, with all their mirth and glee!
This life-long joy, which others had to share
With thee, my brother,—how could I keep from tears?

I seem again thy gentle form to see,
As thou didst sit by me when days were new;
And once more hear thine earnest voice declare:
"There's nothing but what God can do for you."

author: john_masefield
text:
I have brought you here, and now I see
Your life is like the air that falls on thee:
So little that it does not know itself,
And nothing knows but how to let us live!

How much we breathe out for this one breath?
The hour when it was born must never end;
For all the world seems made to serve this nest.
It seems there are no things which do not bend
Towards this alone--it has our love's first light,
It rules from birth, till death comes into sight.

author: matthew_arnold
text:
O God, my Father! when Thou hearest me,
Let not Thy love be blind to my desire;
Nor let it deem that I am but thy child
In name alone, and not by nature tried:
But teach me more than man's belief has learnt,—
That I may feel Thee where Thine angels hurt,
And make no sacrifice too great or small,
If thus I win to do as well as all.

Not so much strength, nor such high-sounding fame,
As this deep heart within me from its pain
Shall pluck for pity

Along some wild and breezy heath, or by-way;
When at the feet of mountain snows I stand,
Or sail among the islands of the sea:
And ever with me shall be held
The memory of our early comradeship.

For me, who never loved the night,
To feel its silence was so hard;
It held no stars nor moon or sun.
Only myself and darkness there;
Though not alone I ne'er had been,
Had not these eyes beheld their beam.

The cold of winter drew my breath,
My body quivered from head to heel.
My thoughts were full of terror now;
No sound except the wind could tell
That life was not destroyed within.
I longed for daylight and would dream
Of waking in the warm sunlight.

Haiku is a form of Japanese poetry, usually written in three lines and 17 syllables total (5-7-5). It can be about anything but often focuses on nature or seasons.

There are no strict rules for how to write one; it's just an exercise in writing creatively and using concise language. Your haiku should use as few words as possible.

text:
For all those nights i’ve slept without knowing day or night,
With only the terror of what lies beyond this fright.
But now there’s someone fighting beside me for my soul,
To show us how even through our darkest moments we can grow.
So as she takes on the battle against her demons each day,
Her courage fills me up with hope once more every time I pray.
She’ll never let darkness win because she has found strength within herself
That shines bright through every single shadow left behind her path--
We're here to support each other

author: sara_teasdale
text:
I see you, my soul,
For you are not alone:
The world is too small
For one to be so tall;
There must be some other--
And he has come at last!

And you have seen his face
While walking among grass;
You can no longer doubt
That this is Love's own son;
He will make your life light,
In spite of all its night.

author: stephen_crane
text:
My Papas

His eyes are all in shadow,
And his back is turned to me:
He has been crying, I know,
Not knowing why or wherefore--
Yet he says nothing, does nothing,
Only keeps quiet and waits.
I have never seen him cry;
But it seems that this will be
The only time he'll ever cry
Before he dies. And when he cries,
It makes my heart ache with pain.

author: christina_rossetti
text:
O God, my Father, King, and Lover,
I have no words to tell how I love thee;
I can but stand and gaze upon thy face;
And with that smile which thou didst give me once,
Thou hast made all things lovely unto me.

I know not what it is to be alone:
Thy hand is ever on mine, and still
It touches me where nothing else can touch,
Even to the hidden secrets of my heart.

author: stephen_crane
text:
The Widow's Lament

I am widowed, all my friends are gathered in a crowd--
To drink and make merry over me, and to laugh at me
Because I have lost him, who was the best of men.
Ah! I weep aloud: I can no longer bear it.
